title: BachelorPad+ Lite: a free Notepad replacement for Windows and Linux
description: A fast, free and open source Notepad replacement for Windows 10, Windows 11 and Linux. Your notes stay as ordinary files, it finds the ones about the same subject, and it never touches the network. GPL-3.0.
keywords: notepad replacement, notepad alternative, text editor, notes app, linux notes, linux text editor, windows notepad alternative, open source text editor, bachelorpad, note taking app, markdown editor, free text editor, offline notes, text editor without AI
h1: Notepad, if Notepad remembered what you wrote.
tagline: Notepad when you want it. More when you need it.
lede: BachelorPad+ Lite is a free, open source Notepad replacement for Windows and Linux. Everything Notepad does, plus one thing it cannot: it knows which of your notes are about the same subject, so you can find last month's thinking without remembering the filename. It opens instantly, works offline forever, and it will never run anything or send anything anywhere.
specimenDoc:
# Quarterly review notes

Three things came up that need a decision before the end of
the month. The pricing one is the only one that is urgent.
whatNote: Everything below works today, in the free version, on Windows and on Linux. There is no account, no sign-in, and no trial period.
card1H: You already know how to use it
card1P: Tabs, find and replace, go to line, undo, zoom, UTF-8, LF or CRLF. If you can use Notepad you can use this, and big files stay quick because editing costs what you changed rather than what the file weighs.
card2H: It names your files for you
card2P: One menu item turns "untitled_3.txt" into Quarterly_Review_10SEP2026.md, taking the title from what you actually wrote. A folder of these sorts itself by date and reads like a list of subjects. You approve every rename before it happens.
card3P: Unsaved changes are kept through a crash, a forced quit or a power cut, and offered back to you next time you open the program. You choose, per document, whether it does this at all.
card4H: It opens instantly and stays out of the way
card4P: One 21 MB download, no runtime to install, no splash screen, no first-run wizard. Unpack it and it runs. Uninstalling is deleting the folder.
card5H: Nothing you type ever leaves your computer
card5P: No telemetry, no update checks, no crash reports, no AI, no account. It behaves identically with the network cable pulled out, and because the source is public you can check that rather than take our word for it.
card6P: There are no scripts, macros or plugins, so a document you were sent cannot do anything when you open it. It also will not grab your file associations or delete anything from your machine without showing you first.
notesH2: The part that is not Notepad: it remembers
notesNote: Open a note and the program quietly learns what it is about. Nothing leaves your machine, your notes stay as ordinary files you can open in anything else, and one setting turns the whole thing off.
note1H: "What else did I write about this?"
note1P: One click lists every note that covers the same ground as the one you are reading, closest first. This is the feature people keep it for: your own thinking from three months ago, found without remembering where you put it.
note2H: It spots when you have written this before
note2P: Save something close to a note you already have, and it tells you, so you end up with one good note instead of four half ones.
note3H: See the shape of everything you have written
note3P: A single report over your whole collection: what you keep coming back to, which notes are stranded and connected to nothing, and what is worth merging. It also tells you what it did not look at, so you know how much to trust it.
notesNotice: All of it is optional and it is off in one setting. The Privacy menu decides whether anything is written down about a document at all. Turn it off and the features say so plainly instead of quietly doing nothing.
privacyH2: Exactly what gets written down, and where
privacyNote: Two things, and nothing else: a recovery file so a crash does not cost you work, and an index entry so the note features work. Both are real trades, so here they are rather than a paragraph of reassurance.
privacyAfter: The menu shows you both of these at all times, so you never have to guess which one you are on. Nothing here is encrypted, and the program says so rather than implying otherwise. Privacy Mode tightens everything for the session and clears recovery files already written.
downloadNote: Version 0.9.5, for Windows 10, Windows 11 and Linux. No installer and no account: unpack the archive wherever you like and run it. Nothing is written outside that folder until you ask.
unsignedNotice: Windows will warn you the first time, and here is why. Code-signing certificates cost money this project does not have yet, so SmartScreen shows a warning. Click "More info", then "Run anyway". Self-signing was rejected because it would ask you to install a root certificate you have no reason to trust, which is worse than a warning.
checksumNote: If you want to confirm the download is the one published, every release ships a checksum file.
platformNote: Windows and Linux, 64-bit. There is no macOS build. macOS would need different file locations, a different way of registering file types, and an Apple certificate before it would open at all. It is not ruled out, but it is not built.
moreH2: The full version arrives in a month
moreNote: Lite is the free half and it stays free. BachelorPad+ is the complete one: encrypted notes, runnable notebooks, structured-data tools, clipboard history and the full privacy controls. It lands on 10 October 2026, and waitlist members hear first and get in early.
colophon1: BachelorPad+ Lite is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 only. It comes with no warranty. Built in Rust with Slint.
colophon2: This page loads no analytics, sets no cookies, and makes no third-party requests. Neither does the program.
donateH2: If it saves you time, you can say thanks
donateNote: BachelorPad+ Lite is free and stays free. There is no paid tier of it, nothing is held back, and nothing nags you. If it has earned a coffee, there is a link.
donateAfter: Donating buys nothing: no priority support, no promised features. If you would rather help without money, report a bug, fix a translation, or tell somebody who is still using Notepad.
wTitle: BachelorPad+: encrypted notes, notebooks and more, arriving October 2026
wDescription: BachelorPad+ is the full version of BachelorPad+ Lite: encrypted notes, runnable notebooks, structured-data tools, clipboard history and complete privacy controls. Arriving 10 October 2026. Join the waitlist for early access.
wKeywords: bachelorpad, encrypted notes, notebook editor, secure text editor, early access, note taking app, offline notes, encrypted notes app
wTagline: Everything Lite does, and the things it cannot.
wLede: Lite gives you a fast editor that remembers what you wrote. BachelorPad+ adds the things you would want next: notes that are actually encrypted, notebooks you can run code in, tools for the messy data files you get sent, and privacy controls that cover everything rather than the essentials. None of it is a mock-up. All of it has been built and run before.
wCaption: until BachelorPad+ arrives, on <time datetime="2026-10-10">10 October 2026</time>. Waitlist members hear first, and get in early.
wWhatH2: What you get that Lite does not give you
wWhatNote: Every item here existed and worked in an earlier version of this program. They were taken out to make Lite small and fast, and they are going back into the full version.
wf1P: Real encryption on a note or a whole folder, with a passphrase you choose. Modern, audited ciphers rather than a password prompt over a plain file. Your crash-recovery files get the same protection, which is the gap most editors leave open.
wf2H: It warns you before you leak a password
wf2P: Paste an API key or a connection string into a note and it tells you where it is, so it does not end up in a screenshot or a shared file. It can black out the sensitive parts, and strip the hidden metadata documents carry around.
wf3P: Write a note, drop in a snippet of Python or SQL, and run it right there, one cell at a time and only when you ask. Jupyter-compatible, so your existing notebooks open and yours open elsewhere.
wf4H: Tidy up messy data files in place
wf4P: Format and check JSON, YAML, TOML and CSV, sort keys, and convert between them without leaving the editor or pasting anything into a website.
wf5P: A searchable clipboard history, and paste that understands what you are pasting into so a table stays a table.
wf6H: Open the log file that crashes other editors
wf6P: Multi-gigabyte files open instantly and read smoothly, because they are streamed from disk instead of loaded whole.
wf7H: Citations and references that stay offline
wf7P: Track sources, identifiers and a reference list inside your notes, with nothing sent to a service and no account required.
wf8P: Four levels covering temporary files, network access, indexing and key storage, not just the two Lite keeps. Set it once and every document follows it.
wNotice: The price is not set yet, and Lite stays free either way. Nothing in Lite will be taken away, moved behind a payment, or turned into a trial. If you only ever use the free version, that is a perfectly good outcome.
wSignupNote: One email when there is something to try, and early access before general release. Nothing else, ever.
wFormNote: Your address is used to email you about BachelorPad+ and nothing else. It is not sold, not shared, and not used to track you. One click in any message removes you.
wFooter: BachelorPad+ Lite is free to download and use right now, under GPL-3.0-only. There is the source code, the downloads, and the manual.
wFooter2: This page loads no analytics, sets no cookies, and stores nothing in your browser.

openH2: Open source, and what it is built on
openNote: Every line is public and licensed under GPL-3.0-only. You can read it, build it, change it, and ship your changes. Nothing is held back in a paid edition of Lite, and there is no contributor agreement that signs your work away.
openWhyH: Why that matters to you and not just to us
openWhyP: This program claims it never touches the network and cannot run anything. Open source is what turns that from a promise into something you can check, by yourself or by anyone you trust. It also means the program cannot be taken away from you: if this project stops, your copy keeps working and somebody else can pick it up.
openBuiltP: BachelorPad+ Lite is built in Rust and would not exist without these projects. The full list of every library in the binary, with its licence, ships inside the download and is in the repository.
openSlint: the user interface toolkit, used under its GPL-3.0 licence
openRopey: the rope that keeps editing fast in large files
openSqlite: SQLite, via rusqlite, holding the note index on your machine
openRfd: native open and save dialogs on both platforms
openTracing: diagnostics, when you ask for them
openContribP: Bug reports are the most useful thing, and the issue templates ask for the few details that make a report fixable. Translations, documentation fixes and code are all welcome. If you just want the thing to succeed, telling one person who still uses Notepad does more than you would think.
consentReleases: Email me when a new version of BachelorPad+ Lite is released. My address is stored in Ireland and sent to Kit, who send the mail. I can unsubscribe from any message.
consentWaitlist: Email me about BachelorPad+ early access. My address is stored in Ireland and sent to Kit, who send the mail. I can unsubscribe from any message.
jsNeedConsent: Please tick the box to confirm you want these emails.
pDescription: What bpad.prompt-forge.dev collects, which is one email address if you ask for one of the two mailing lists, and nothing otherwise. The program itself collects nothing at all.
pLede: This page collects nothing unless you type an address into one of the two forms and tick the box. The program collects nothing at all, ever.
pProductH: The program, first, because it is the part most people are asking about
pProductP: BachelorPad+ Lite makes no network connection. There is no telemetry, no update check, no crash reporting, no AI and no account. It behaves identically on a computer that has never been online, and because the source is public you can confirm that rather than take it on trust. What it writes on your own machine is your choice and is set out in the manual, under Privacy.
pCollectH: What this website collects, why, and on what legal basis
pRow1Data: Email address, which of the two lists you chose, the date, and the exact wording you agreed to
pRow1Purpose: Sending you release notes, or telling you BachelorPad+ early access has opened
pRow2Data: Whatever you write in an email or a public issue
pRow2Kept: Until it is no longer useful
pCollectAfter: Giving an address is entirely voluntary and nothing here is required of you. If you would rather give nobody an address, watch releases on GitHub instead; it is the same information. The two lists are separate, and joining one does not join the other.
pCookiesP: There are none, and there is no banner because there is nothing to consent to. This site sets no cookies, stores nothing in your browser, loads no analytics and makes no third-party requests. A Content-Security-Policy of self means your browser would refuse one, and the build fails if anybody adds one, so this is enforced rather than promised.
pProcessorsH: Who else handles it, and where
pProcessorsP: Your address is stored in Microsoft Azure Table Storage in Ireland, and passed to Kit (formerly ConvertKit) in the United States, who send the mail and handle unsubscribes. Nobody else receives it. It is not sold, not shared and not used to build a profile of you.
pRightsP: You can ask for a copy of what is held, ask for it to be corrected or deleted, withdraw consent, or object. The quickest route to deletion is the unsubscribe link in any message, which removes you without anybody reading the request first. Otherwise write to business@prompt-forge.dev. If you are in the EEA or the UK you may also complain to your national data protection authority.
pChildrenP: This is a text editor for people doing their own work, and nothing here is aimed at children. No address is knowingly collected from anyone under 16.
pChangesP: The consent wording is versioned, and records keep the wording that was actually agreed to rather than being rewritten to the newest text. If this page changes materially, anyone on a list is told before it takes effect.
